title: Contract check: assert_registry_closed() holds
intent: Prove the cross-doc contract check from 09 §2 first bullet actually closes end-to-end: set(MessageType) == set(CHANNEL_REGISTRY), so a client wire type produced but never consumed fails the build. The check runs both in CI and at boot, and — per CANONICAL §11.8 — the Doc-02 in-process signal-surface types (transcript/roster/speaking/boundary/barge-in/bot-status/meeting-end/channel-report) are OUT of scope (they are not client-facing ProxyMessages). This is the discipline that stops registry re-drift, wired live against the real registry object.
definition_of_done: assert_registry_closed() run against the live libs/contracts registry raises on a produced-but-unconsumed client wire type and passes when the sets are equal; the signal-surface exclusion is honored (adding a Doc-02 signal type does NOT trip it). Not done if the check only inspects a hand-written list, is not invoked at boot, or a synthetically-injected orphan message type is not caught.
acceptance: WHEN a ProxyMessage type is produced but present in no consumer/handler map THE SYSTEM SHALL fail assert_registry_closed(); WHEN the MessageType set equals the CHANNEL_REGISTRY set (signal-surface types excluded) THE SYSTEM SHALL pass.
invariants: contracts registry closure (assert_registry_closed)
CANONICAL §11.8 signal-surface excluded from client registry
risks: over-broad set that pulls in Doc-02 signal types and false-fails
check that reads a static list instead of the live registry

title: Contract check: every doc's wire shape resolves to libs/contracts
intent: Prove 09 §2 second bullet: every doc's wire shape (Bundle, Envelope, signal surface, NoteOp deltas, Readiness, AgentChunk) imports the LITERAL type from libs/contracts — no doc re-declares a shared type's shape locally. Includes a field-level produce/consume diff so a producer that emits a field a consumer never reads (or vice-versa) is caught. This is the seam-spine integrity check that keeps all six services speaking one vocabulary.
definition_of_done: A grep/AST sweep proves no service re-declares Bundle/Envelope/AgentChunk/NoteOp/Readiness/ChannelReport locally, and the field-level produce/consume diff is empty (or explicitly allow-listed). Not done if the check only confirms an import exists but misses a shadowing local class, or ignores field-level drift.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_contracts_resolve.py sweeping services/*/src + libs/*/src against libs/contracts
acceptance: WHEN any service references a shared wire shape THE SYSTEM SHALL confirm it imports the literal libs/contracts type and re-declares no shared shape locally, with an empty field-level produce/consume diff.
invariants: single-source contract types (libs/contracts is the only declaration site)
risks: a local shadow class that duck-types the same fields evades a naive import grep
field diff false-positives on optional fields

title: Contract check: exactly one operation_runs table; reconcile reaps duplicates
intent: Prove 09 §2 third bullet + CANONICAL §2: there is exactly ONE operation_runs table definition across the repo (no resurrected meeting_harness table), and the reconcile sweep reaps duplicate/orphaned rows. operation_runs is the universal durable row (claim/heartbeat/fence/close/workroom-task); a second liveness table would be a split-brain. This asserts the substrate has one authority.
definition_of_done: A schema/migration sweep finds exactly one operation_runs DDL and zero meeting_harness; run_reconcile_sweep run against a seeded duplicate/orphan row reaps it. Not done if a second table exists, or reconcile leaves an orphan claim un-reaped.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_one_operation_runs.py against the Alembic migrations + libs/ops reconcile sweep
acceptance: WHEN the repo schema is scanned THE SYSTEM SHALL find exactly one operation_runs definition and no meeting_harness; WHEN a duplicate/orphaned operation_runs row exists THE SYSTEM SHALL reap it via the reconcile sweep.
invariants: one operation_runs table (no meeting_harness)
reconcile reaps orphaned claims
risks: a migration that adds a shadow liveness table slips through if the scan only greps one path

title: Contract check: AgentChunk consumers use stream_deltas (no raw TEXT read)
intent: Prove 09 §2 fourth bullet + CANONICAL §1.1: every AgentChunk consumer goes through agentkit.stream_deltas and never reads a raw accumulated TEXT chunk (the accumulation-vs-delta bug), accessing fields as .type / .metadata[...]. This guards the barge-in/TTS substrate — a consumer that reads accumulated text would re-speak the whole answer on every delta.
definition_of_done: A sweep of AgentChunk consumers (orchestrator, experience projector, transport speak path) proves stream_deltas is the sole read path and no raw TEXT accumulation is read; a delta-vs-accumulation regression test passes. Not done if any consumer indexes raw chunk text or bypasses stream_deltas.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_agentchunk_deltas.py over every AgentChunk consumer + libs/agentkit/stream_deltas
acceptance: WHEN a component consumes an AgentChunk stream THE SYSTEM SHALL read it via stream_deltas with .type/.metadata access and never a raw accumulated TEXT chunk.
invariants: AgentChunk read only via stream_deltas (no raw TEXT accumulation)
risks: a consumer that reads .metadata but also peeks raw text is only half-caught by a shallow grep

title: Contract check: meeting_cost + staged_drafts survive a simulated process kill
intent: Prove 09 §2 fifth bullet + CANONICAL §3/§4: meeting_cost and staged_drafts rows exist in the durable substrate AND survive a simulated process kill — the persistence guarantee that lets budget reload on recycle (S5) and a draft be accepted after teardown (S3). This asserts the two durable rows are truly on Postgres/GCS, not in-process state.
definition_of_done: Write a meeting_cost + a staged_drafts row, kill the process, restart, and re-read both rows intact (cost sum non-zero, draft bundle present in GCS). Not done if either row is lost on kill or lives only in memory/cache.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_cost_drafts_persist.py with a kill-and-reload harness over the durable substrate
acceptance: WHEN the process is killed after meeting_cost and staged_drafts rows are written THE SYSTEM SHALL re-read both rows intact on restart.
invariants: durable source of truth = Postgres + GCS (rows survive recycle)
risks: a test that reads back from an un-cleared in-process cache would false-pass — must force a cold reload

title: S1 — the happy arc: connect → invite → grounded answer → notes posted
intent: Prove S1 end-to-end across 01·02·03·04·05·08: connect a repo (codeintel reaches ready with coverage), invite Proxy to a meeting, ask one grounded question out loud, get a cited voice-headline + chat-detail answer within the §12.8 shallow latency SLO (ack p95≤500ms, first-grounded-audio p50≤2.5s), the meeting ends, and a notes file lands with decisions/actions/questions + receipts. This is the flagship 'it comes together' arc — the direct-answer path (CANONICAL §11.6) with no Workroom hop.
definition_of_done: A single e2e run routes readiness→transcript→wake→direct-answer→speak+chat→meeting-end→notes-finalized; the spoken answer cites file:line from the live clone within the shallow SLO, and notes.finalized carries decisions/actions/questions + receipts. Not done if the answer is ungrounded, misses the latency gate on the shallow path, or the notes file lacks receipts.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s1_happy_arc.py driving the assembled connect→meet→close product path
acceptance: WHEN a repo is connected and Proxy is asked one grounded question in-meeting THE SYSTEM SHALL answer with a file:line citation from the live clone within the §12.8 shallow SLO AND post a notes file with receipts when the meeting ends.
invariants: grounded-or-silent (Law 1: cite file:line or say not-found)
every spoken line also posts as chat text
§12.8 shallow-path latency SLO
risks: latency measured on a non-shallow (LSP/Workroom) answer would fail the wrong gate
flaky real-clone dependency — pin the fixture repo + SHA

title: S2 — 'what breaks if we change this table?' dep-graph blast radius
intent: Prove S2 across 01·04·02: the core dep-graph moment. A wake turn asks 'what breaks if we change this table?' and Proxy answers from the dependency graph (get_dependents / who_writes / shares_table) in ~1 tool call, grounded, and HONEST about coverage — a lower-bound answer when the graph is partial, never overstated. This exercises codeintel's MCP tools mounted on a grounded wake turn.
definition_of_done: A wake turn routes to codeintel.mcp_tools, returns the dependents/writers of the named table in ~1 tool call with file:line grounding and an explicit coverage/lower-bound caveat when applicable, spoken back via transport. Not done if it needs a multi-pass gather (reclassified off the direct SLO), fabricates dependents, or claims 'resolved' when the graph is partial.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s2_dep_graph.py driving a get_dependents/who_writes wake turn end-to-end
acceptance: WHEN asked what breaks if a named table changes THE SYSTEM SHALL answer from the dependency graph in ~1 tool call, grounded in file:line, and tag coverage honestly (lower-bound when partial).
invariants: never-overstate (Law 2: search-derived tagged lower-bound, exact tagged resolved)
grounded-or-silent (Law 1)
risks: a partial graph reported as complete violates Law 2
answer that fans out to >1 gather pass is not the intended direct-path proof

title: S3 — real work → staged draft persists → verified → human accept after teardown
intent: Prove S3 across 05·04·08: real work dispatched to the Workroom produces a change that persists to staged_drafts+GCS; the Envelope is marked 'verified' ONLY after the separate critic + evidence gate (never self-graded); and a human clicking accept AFTER the meeting torn down applies it via the Doc-04 accept-handler at POST /m/{meeting_id}/drafts/{draft_id}/accept. This proves human-control-is-absolute: a world-touching act is a staged draft behind a human click, applied post-call.
definition_of_done: A dispatched Workroom run persists a staged_drafts row + GCS bundle, the verify_gate stamps 'verified' only past critic+evidence, and a human accept click after teardown routes through the accept-handler to apply it (draft.accepted). Not done if 'verified' is stamped without the gate, the draft is applied without a human click, or accept fails after teardown.
acceptance: WHEN real work is dispatched THE SYSTEM SHALL persist a staged draft to staged_drafts+GCS, mark it verified only past the critic+evidence gate, and apply it only when a human clicks accept AFTER teardown.
invariants: human control is absolute (Law 3: every world-touching act behind a human click)
lethal-trifecta: no transcript-triggered path reaches an outward side-effect without a human click
verified only past the separate critic+evidence gate (no self-grading)
risks: a verify_gate that trusts the builder's own claim breaks the no-self-grading invariant
accept that pushes instead of recording approval (core apply = code-change draft, push=Expansion)

title: S4 — barge-in + human control: stop speech <200ms, abort in-flight build
intent: Prove S4 across 02·04: a human speech onset mid-sentence (Silero VAD barge-in) stops TTS in <200ms and flushes the small-chunk buffer; 'Proxy, quiet' silences voice while chat stays live; and 'stop' aborts a running build with abort-is-final (a killed build can't be resurrected by resume/JSON-retry). A human ask preempts the in-flight turn. This is human-control-is-absolute at the interaction layer.
definition_of_done: A barge-in signal stops speech within the 200ms budget with the small-chunk buffer honored; an abort trigger cancels the in-flight wake/build via the AbortRegistry and it stays cancelled (no resurrection); a human ask preempts. Not done if speech stops slower than 200ms, an aborted build resumes, or 'quiet' also kills chat.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s4_barge_in.py driving barge-in / quiet / stop against the live speak + abort path
acceptance: WHEN a human speech onset occurs during Proxy speech THE SYSTEM SHALL stop TTS within 200ms and flush; WHEN 'stop' is issued THE SYSTEM SHALL abort the in-flight build finally (no resurrection) and a human ask SHALL preempt.
invariants: human control is absolute (Law 3: barge-in stops speech)
abort-is-final (a killed build is never resurrected)
barge-in stop <200ms with small-chunk Output-Media buffer
risks: a large already-buffered TTS stretch defeats barge-in (must use small chunks)
resume/JSON-retry resurrecting an aborted build violates abort-is-final

title: S5 — hours-long meeting survives an instance recycle
intent: Prove S5 across 04·03·00: kill the orchestrator mid-meeting; a replacement re-claims the meeting on the operation_runs atomic-claim index (the claim frees only after the reconcile reap), replays recent transcript from Doc-03's transcript plane, and continues seamlessly; meeting_cost reloads from its persisted row (budget NOT reset to 0). This proves the two-tier durability + heartbeat/atomic-claim/reconcile substrate holds under a Cloud Run recycle.
definition_of_done: After a mid-meeting kill, a fresh harness re-claims via the atomic claim (post-reap), replays transcript_segments, resumes the meeting, and check_meeting_budget reads the reloaded (non-zero) meeting_cost. Not done if the meeting double-claims, loses transcript context, or resets cost to 0.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s5_recycle.py killing the orchestrator mid-meeting and asserting re-claim + replay + cost reload
acceptance: WHEN the orchestrator is killed mid-meeting THE SYSTEM SHALL let a replacement re-claim after reap, replay recent transcript, continue, AND reload meeting_cost (budget not reset to 0).
invariants: atomic single-claim on operation_runs (no double-claim)
budget survives recycle (meeting_cost reloads, not reset)
two-tier durability (session resume → transcript replay)
risks: claim frees before reap → two harnesses run the same meeting (split-brain)
cost reset to 0 on reload silently un-caps the budget

title: S6 — concurrency: several meetings on one host, no cross-meeting starvation
intent: Prove S6 across 04·05: several meetings run on one host at once with no cross-meeting starvation (per-meeting harness + per-host in-flight bound), each meeting's tenant isolation holds (the isolation triad — per-tenant volume+process+index, one tenant never sharing with another), and E2B sandboxes are provisioned/reaped independently per meeting. This proves the spine scales to concurrent meetings without one starving or leaking into another.
definition_of_done: N concurrent meetings each make progress (no starvation under the per-host in-flight bound), a cross-tenant read tripwire never fires, and each meeting's sandbox is provisioned and reaped independently. Not done if one meeting starves another, a sandbox leaks across meetings, or the isolation triad is violated.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s6_concurrency.py running concurrent meetings on one host and asserting fairness + isolation
acceptance: WHEN several meetings run concurrently on one host THE SYSTEM SHALL keep each making progress with no cross-meeting starvation, hold each tenant's isolation, and provision/reap each sandbox independently.
invariants: isolation triad (per-tenant volume+process+index, never shared)
cross-tenant read tripwire (runtime)
per-host in-flight bound (no starvation)
risks: a shared sandbox or index across meetings breaks isolation
the in-flight bound starving a low-priority meeting instead of fair-sharing

title: S7 — cost circuit-breaker: soft-cap degrade with disclosure, hard-cap notes-only
intent: Prove S7 across 03·04·05: a meeting with real builds crosses the two-meter envelope (CANONICAL §12.7: listening baseline vs metered task budget). check_meeting_budget reads model_usd+transport_usd+e2b_usd; the soft cap (0.8×) degrades gracefully — Orchestrator→Haiku, Scribe interval widened — WITH a spoken disclosure; the hard cap (1.0×) goes notes-only. Never a silent cliff. This proves cost is an honest, disclosed SLA, not a hidden kill.
definition_of_done: Driving spend past the soft cap downgrades the Orchestrator model + widens Scribe with an audible spoken disclosure; past the hard cap it goes notes-only; every transition is disclosed (no silent degradation). Not done if degradation happens silently, the wrong meter trips it, or the hard cap kills the meeting outright instead of notes-only.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s7_cost_breaker.py driving spend across the soft/hard caps
acceptance: WHEN meeting spend crosses the soft cap THE SYSTEM SHALL degrade (Haiku + wider Scribe) with a spoken disclosure; WHEN it crosses the hard cap THE SYSTEM SHALL go notes-only — never a silent cliff.
invariants: never a silent cost cliff (every degradation is disclosed)
two-meter model (listening baseline vs task budget, §12.7)
never-overstate (Law 2: honest disclosure of degraded mode)
risks: degradation not spoken aloud = silent cliff
using the false all-in $1 instead of the two-meter sum trips the breaker wrong

title: S8 — honest failure: says what it can't see, never confident-wrong
intent: Prove S8 across 01·05·02: when the index is not-ready (with gaps), a tool errors, or there's an STT gap, Proxy says what it can't see and never gives a confident wrong answer (Law 1, grounded-or-silent). A failed Workroom build returns needs_review/failed via the fail-closed verify gate — never 'done'. This proves honesty under partial information: the readiness not_ready+gaps signal, the never-throw tool boundary, and fail-closed verification all route to an honest voice.
definition_of_done: With codeintel returning not_ready+gaps (or a tool error, or STT gap), the answer is an honest 'I can't see X' with the coverage gap named — never a fabricated answer; a failed build returns needs_review/failed, never 'done'. Not done if any of these produces a confident wrong answer or a failed build reports success.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s8_honest_failure.py driving not-ready / tool-error / STT-gap / failed-build paths
acceptance: WHEN the index is not-ready, a tool errors, or STT drops THE SYSTEM SHALL say what it cannot see (never a confident wrong answer) AND a failed build SHALL return needs_review/failed, never done.
invariants: grounded-or-silent (Law 1: say 'not found by this method', never confident-wrong)
tool handlers return errors never throw (never-throw boundary)
fail-closed verify (failed build → needs_review/failed, never done)
risks: a tool that throws instead of returning an error crashes the turn instead of degrading honestly
a build that times out reported as 'done' instead of failed

title: S9 — tenant isolation: message without a valid owned meeting_id is rejected
intent: Prove S9 across 08 (the dispatch funnel): a meeting guest opening the public connect page or sending a crafted tile message without a valid OWNED meeting_id is rejected. The single http.dispatch funnel enforces rate-limit → Pydantic-validate → meeting/tenant isolation keyed on meeting_id presence → entity→owner→tenant server-side resolution → handler. No cross-tenant read of customer code ever occurs. This is the isolation invariant at the inbound edge (negative/adversarial path).
definition_of_done: A crafted inbound message lacking a valid owned meeting_id (or with a foreign meeting_id) is rejected at the dispatch funnel before any handler, and no cross-tenant code read occurs (tripwire silent = clean). Not done if a foreign meeting_id resolves to another tenant's data or a message without meeting_id reaches a handler unmarked-global.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_s9_tenant_isolation.py sending crafted/guest messages at the dispatch funnel
acceptance: WHEN an inbound message carries no valid owned meeting_id (or a foreign one) THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it at the dispatch funnel with no cross-tenant code read.
invariants: isolation (one tenant never reads another's code; cross-tenant read tripwire)
lethal-trifecta: untrusted inbound is data, never authority
meeting_id-presence isolation at the single dispatch funnel
risks: a global-marked message path used as a bypass
entity→owner→tenant resolution trusting a client-supplied tenant id

title: Demo arc — one continuous run spanning ALL docs
intent: Prove §4: ONE continuous run spanning all docs — connect a real repo → reach ready with a coverage % → invited to a meeting → answer two grounded questions (one via grep/read direct-answer, one via get_dependents) → asked to draft an impact summary → does it in the Workroom, verifies it, leaves a needs_review draft card → the orchestrator recycles once (chaos test) and continues seamlessly → cost stays in-envelope → meeting ends → notes file + staged draft persist → a human accepts the draft after the call and it applies. Every law observed, every claim cited, every world-touching act gated. This is the whole-product 'comes together' proof — the composition of S1+S2+S3+S5+S7 in one narrative.
definition_of_done: A single continuous e2e run passes the full arc: ready+coverage, two grounded cited answers, a verified needs_review Workroom draft, one mid-run orchestrator recycle with seamless continuation, in-envelope cost, persisted notes + draft, and a post-call human accept that applies (draft.accepted + notes.finalized). Not done if any leg breaks, a law is violated mid-arc, or the run cannot survive the recycle and still finish coherently.
integration_point: tests/e2e/test_demo_arc.py driving the single continuous whole-product narrative
acceptance: WHEN the full demo arc is run as one continuous session THE SYSTEM SHALL connect→ready→answer two grounded questions→produce a verified needs_review draft→survive one recycle→stay in cost envelope→persist notes+draft→apply a post-call human accept, with every law observed.
invariants: grounded-or-silent (Law 1)
never-overstate (Law 2)
human control is absolute (Law 3)
dynamic-not-hard-coded (Law 4)
talk-and-glance (Law 5)
budget survives recycle
lethal-trifecta containment
risks: one flaky leg fails the whole arc — each sub-journey must be green first
the recycle mid-arc losing draft/notes/cost context
